A CLAIM BUILT ON A NAME IS LEFT STANDING AGAINST A LIST THAT DOES NOT CARRY IT [claim G59-27]. The bride at 28:9 was read as named for the forgiveness of the groom's iniquities; in this roster the same woman appears under a different name. The chain records the shift rather than harmonizing it. [folded shape: recorded dispute]

A MIGRATION READ AS EVASION OF A RECORDED OBLIGATION [claim G59-24]. He went to another land DUE TO his brother - and the cause is read as the promissory note: he left the Land to escape the servitude clause of the covenant, the four hundred years his descendants would otherwise owe. A departure verse turned into a claim about who bears a debt the text recorded four blocks earlier. Onkelos separat…

THE OTHER BROTHER'S DWELL [care 4]. va-YESHEV esav be-har seir (3427 tok52/199; 8165 tok5/20) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.8] — Esau performs in one clause the dwell-verb that gen_58's shev-card still holds open for Jacob (whose narrator got shakhan instead): the brothers' inverse compliance, letter-note only. esav HU EDOM — equation #2. No etnachta (the span's one zaqef-qatan fallback).

THE ONLY DOUBLED TOLEDOT [CROWN 5]. ve-ele TOLDOT esav AVI edom be-har seir (8435 tok12/29) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.9; full census] — the generations-formula repeats for the same man: no other subject in the Torah carries two headers — Canaan's Esau (36:1-8) and Seir's (36:9-43), the letter splitting the life at the mountain; and the epithet shifts with it: hu edom ("he IS Edom") becomes avi ed…

THE NAME-LIST OPENS. ele SHEMOT bene esav (8034 tok91/252) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.10] — the shem-noun heads a list that WRITES nothing: dozens of names mentioned, no va-yiqra act anywhere in the chapter — the registry sleeps through the Torah's densest name-field [UNIT SHAPE]. Each son tagged by mother: ben ada eshet esav, ben basmat eshet esav.

A LIST OF NAMES TREATED AS AN EVIDENTIARY DOCUMENT [claim G59-23]. The roster is peeled like an onion - I have exposed his hidden places - specifically to expose the illegitimate births, with the number disputed at three against four, and one name identified as such because it stands in two incompatible lines. A standing credit adds a second exhibit, one figure listed both as brother and as son of…

AMALEK WITH A TITLE [CROWN 4]. aluf qorach aluf gatam aluf AMALEQ (6002 tok2/14) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.16] — Amalek's second and last Genesis token wears the chief-title; his next appearance is the war at Refidim (Exod 17:8). ele alufe elifaz be-eretz edom.

THE SECOND FOUR TITLED. aluf nachat aluf zerach aluf shama aluf miza — Reuel's four each take the title (441 toks 10-13/44) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.17]; the mother-tag closes the list as it closed 36:13.

KORACH TITLED [care 2]. aluf yeush aluf yalam aluf QORACH (7141 tok4/21) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.18] — the Edomite Korach's last token wears the chief-title; the name's next bearer (tok5, Exod 6:21) is born to Levi and dies in Num 16's earth.

EQUATION #3 [CROWN 5]. ele vene esav ve-ele ALUFEHEM hu EDOM [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.19] — the sons-and-chiefs ledger seals with the identity-clause's third saying. No etnachta (tifcha split, fallback #4).

SEVEN NATIVE CHIEFS. ve-dishon ve-etzer ve-dishan — Seir's seven sons (441 toks continue) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.21] — the chief-title covers the natives too: Edom's ledger grants the Horites the same rank-word it grants Esau's line.

THE LIST RUNS. ve-ele bene shoval [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.23] — five Horite grandsons; the ledger's rhythm holds.

THE TRANSLATION HOLDS A LEXICAL SEAT OF ITS OWN [claim G59-28]. What was found in the wilderness is disputed between mules and hot springs; Onkelos renders THE MIGHTY ONES - giants. A third reading of a word that occurs once, entered without argument. Elsewhere in this sweep the buffer votes in the chain's disputes; here it opens one. [folded shape: dual-track translation]

THE WIFE'S PEDIGREE CONFIRMED. ve-ele vene ana dishon ve-AHOLIVAMA bat ana (173 tok6/7) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.25] — Esau's third wife stands in the Horite line: the marriage crossed into the native list, as Timna's concubinage crossed out of it — the two ledgers trade one woman each.
THE LIST RUNS ON. ve-ele bene dishan [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.26] — four entries; the rhythm holds.
THE SEVENTH HOUSE NEARS. ele bene etzer [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.27] — three entries; one Horite house remains.

UTZ CLOSES. ele vene dishan UTZ va-aran (5780 tok3/3 CLOSES) [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.28] — the name's three Torah tokens sit in three houses: Aram's son (10:23, Shem's line), Nachor's firstborn (22:21, Abraham's kin), and the Horite here — one name across three nations (the Korach pattern widened). No etnachta (tifcha split, fallback #5).

THE NATIVE TITLES. ele alufe ha-chori [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.29] — the seven Horite heads take the aluf-title in their own right (441 toks 21-25 in this verse; the seven head-titles run toks 22-28 across 36:29-30).

BY THEIR CHIEFDOMS. ele alufe ha-chori LE-ALUFEHEM be-eretz seir [VERIFIED: SNAPSHOT Gen.36.30] — the title doubled into a collective ("by their chiefdoms") — the Horite ledger seals in Seir's name as Esau's sealed in Edom's (36:19).

THE PENALTY SPOKEN AT GEN_55 IS COUNTED AT THIS VERSE, AND BOTH NUMBERS ARE EIGHT [claim G59-21, machine-checked]. The chain sets Edom's eight named kings against Israel's eight and states the alternation rule: when one crowns kings the other appoints judges, chieftains against princes, until a later empire scrambles both. Our ink carries both ends - the deference stands exactly eight times across…

A GENEALOGY READ AS A CONSTITUTIONAL CLAIM [claim G59-22]. Their kings come from elsewhere - one from one town, one from a river-city - mast from one place and anchors from another: no dynasty and no soil. The estate seized hastily at the start is read as these kings who reigned before Israel had any, its end left unblessed. [folded shape: kept record]

A COMMERCIAL LIABILITY RULE TRANSPOSED TO STATECRAFT [claim G59-25]. I will contend only with the city that supplied the king - the supplier of a ruler being liable for him, carried by a parable about who sustains whom, and seated on the one king in this list whose town of origin is named. [folded shape: priced law]

A remaining-count and an escrow, taken from the last lines of a genealogy. Onkelos separately reads one name as a trade where …
